newsitem.title: NORWAY: Russia's Primakov arrives in Norway for NATO talks.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Primakov arrives in Norway for NATO talks.

text.p: Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov arrived on Monday for talks with Norwegian leaders on NATO's enlargement plans and other issues, Norwegian officials said.
Primakov, starting a two-day official visit, flew in from Brussels where he discussed NATO's eastward enlargement with NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana on Sunday.
Primakov, who rode in a motorcade from Fornebu airport into
Oslo, was due to meet parliament president Kirsti Kolle Groendahl before holding talks with Foreign Minister Bjoern Godal, Defence Minister Joergen Kosmo and Environment Minister Torbjoern Berntsen.
"With Primakov coming straight from Brussels there is no doubt they will discuss NATO's enlargement," Foreign Ministry spokesman Ingvard Havnen said.
While NATO insists it will not let Moscow have a veto over who can join the alliance, it has offered a range of measures to try to reassure Russia that the admission of former Soviet
satellites on its western flank will not be a security threat.
Other issues likely to come up in Oslo were the Middle East peace process and Yugoslavia as well as bilateral cooperation in the Arctic, Havnen said.
Norway is the only NATO member to share a border with Russia.
Godal and Primakov planned to hold a joint news conference at 3.30 P.M. (1430gmt).
Primakov will meet Prime Minister Thorbjoern Jagland on Tuesday before leaving Norway.
